abstract: The Synthetic Chemical Exposome Database (SynCED) (https://syncedb.ca) is a substantially updated and expanded version of the Toxin and Toxin Target Database (T3DB). SynCED provides rich data on 316 418 synthetic chemicals from diverse chemical, toxicological, exposure, and regulatory sources. The synthetic chemical exposome comprises a vast and rapidly expanding range of anthropogenic chemicals, yet information on their sources, uses, biological effects, toxicity, and molecular interactions remains fragmented across numerous resources. SynCED addresses this problem by consolidating this information and linking most known synthetic chemicals with standardized chemical names and identifiers, compound descriptions, predicted or measured physicochemical properties, reference spectral data, exposure and use information, toxicological data, and biological targets or interactions. Literature-derived compound descriptions and functional annotations were built using the Chemical Functional Ontology (ChemFOnt) Fact Finder pipeline, which extracts semantically defined chemical-relation-entity associations while retaining supporting evidence and provenance. In addition to literature-derived biological target information, SynCED also incorporates ligand-based protein-target predictions to extend the coverage of chemicals lacking experimentally characterized interactions. To facilitate compound identification using non-target or suspect screening, SynCED provides extensive search utilities supporting searches by chemical structure, toxicity, text, mass, molecular weight, elemental composition, ESI-MS, EI-MS, and NMR spectra (both measured and predicted) as well as searches by target sequence (protein and DNA). It also supports database browsing by chemical names, ClassyFire chemical taxonomy and exposure source. Together, these features extend T3DB to turn SynCED into a broader, more provenance-aware database, that supports suspect or non-target screening, chemical exposure and hazard assessment, mechanistic studies, and general chemical exposomics research.
